title: California's 7th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 7th Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, featuring a unique Democratic-versus-Democratic contest under California's top-two primary system. Incumbent Congresswoman Doris Matsui, who has represented the Sacramento area since 2005, faces a progressive challenge from Sacramento City Councilmember Mai Vang, who narrowly led the June 2, 2026 primary. The district was significantly redrawn under Proposition 50 and now includes Sacramento, Elk Grove, Galt, Lodi, Placerville, and El Dorado. The race centers on a generational and ideological contrast, with Matsui emphasizing her seniority and record of delivering federal funding, while Vang advocates for Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and rejecting corporate PAC contributions.
polling_note: No public general-election polls were found for CA-07 as of this report, though the New York Times maintains a tracking page for the district.

candidates.name: Doris Matsui
candidates.summary: Doris Matsui has represented California's 7th Congressional District (and its predecessor districts) in the U.S. House since 2005. A senior member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, she serves as Ranking Member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee and has authored major legislation including the CHIPS for America Act. She emphasizes her record of securing over $4 billion for Sacramento-area flood protection, helping craft the Affordable Care Act, and delivering federal infrastructure investments.

candidates.name: Mai Vang
candidates.summary: Mai Vang is a Sacramento City Councilmember representing District 8, first elected in 2020. She is the daughter of Hmong refugees, the eldest of 16 children, and a former community organizer who co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics. Vang advocates for progressive policies including Medicare for All, affordable housing, abolishing ICE, and rejecting corporate PAC donations, and she has positioned herself as a new-generation alternative to the incumbent.
